hooks.text: A four-pound rock from Mars prompted an address by President Bill Clinton.
Why did a single Antarctic rock trigger a televised US presidential address?
President Bill Clinton addressed the world over one four-pound Martian rock.

title: The President's Martian Rock
description: Discover how a four-pound meteorite found in Antarctica sparked a global debate and a presidential address about life on Mars.

beats.text: A four-pound rock from Mars prompted an address by President Bill Clinton.
beats.visual: photograph of President Bill Clinton delivering his 1996 meteorite speech, White House, 1996

beats.text: In December 1984, an American expedition searching the Allan Hills of Antarctica collected the unusual stone as their team's very first find.
beats.visual: photograph of the Allan Hills icefield in Antarctica, ANSMET field team, 1984

beats.text: A violent asteroid impact had blasted this ancient crust directly off the Martian surface around sixteen million years ago.
beats.visual: artist's concept of a large asteroid hitting the Martian surface, 2020

beats.text: After drifting through the solar system, the wandering meteorite crashed into the Antarctic ice sheet approximately thirteen thousand years ago.
beats.visual: diagram of a meteorite's interplanetary transit path from Mars to Earth, 2020

beats.text: In 1996, NASA scientists led by David McKay announced the rock might contain fossilized life, triggering a televised presidential address.
beats.visual: scanning electron microscope image of ALH 84001 microscopic structures, NASA, 1996

beats.text: Scientists later proved these shapes were just unusual geology, yet history still remembers that presidential address.
beats.visual: photograph of the ALH 84001 meteorite specimen, NASA Johnson Space Center, 1996
